text:
Senator Doug Mastriano marks key historical anniversaries in September social media posts
B. L. Sexton
Pennsylvania State Senator Doug Mastriano, who serves Adams and Franklin counties and has a record of supporting veterans through legislative and community initiatives, marked several significant historical anniversaries in recent posts on his official X account.
On September 1, 2026, Mastriano posted: "September 1st, 1752 - The Liberty Bell arrived in Philadelphia. https://t.co/6jzH1iRm96".
Later that day, he noted the start of World War II with the post: "September 1st, 1939 - WW2 began https://t.co/J1vnppTCFR".
On September 2, 2026, Mastriano commemorated the end of World War II by writing: "September 2nd, 1945 - WW2 ended - President Harry Truman declared V-J Day (Victory over Japan Day) commemorating the formal Japanese surrender to the Allies aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay. https://t.co/R4UYKVpFsW".
Senator Mastriano’s focus on military history aligns with his role as chairman of both the Senate Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committee and the Senate Local Government Committee. His public service record includes advancing veteran support efforts through legislation and community engagement as part of his work within Pennsylvania state governance (official website).
